defects.match: return a.ID == b.ID && a.Owner == b.Owner && a.Currency == b.Currency && a.Balance == b.Balance
defects.note: Equal compares four of the five fields; a freeze or unfreeze is a change the reconciler never sees, so a frozen account stays active downstream
Clone copies Entries but not Totals; the renderer's annotations land in the map the store handed out
len counts bytes and MaxMemo is documented in characters; a 71-letter Cyrillic memo is 142 bytes and is refused. utf8.RuneCountInString
the +5000 half-up bias and Go's truncating division both push a negative amount toward zero: Fee(-30, 250) is 0 where the doc promises -Fee(30, 250) = -1; round the magnitude and reapply the sign
strings.Split("", ",") is [""], one empty id, so the documented empty list fails in ParseInt instead of selecting every account

the map key compares PostedAt with ==, which also compares Location and the monotonic reading; the store's rows and the importer's parsed batch carry the same instant in different locations, so no replayed entry is ever a duplicate. Key on UnixNano, or compare with Equal
AddDate normalizes: January 31 plus one month is March 3, not the last day of February the doc promises; clamp the day to the following month's length
Truncate works on the absolute time since the zero instant, which is midnight UTC; for Kyiv it returns 03:00 local. time.Date(y, m, d, 0, 0, 0, 0, loc) is the local midnight

defects.match: {name: "small refund carries no fee", amount: -30, bps: 250, want: 0},
defects.note: the expectation encodes the rounding defect: by Fee's own contract a -30 refund carries a fee of -1, and the case name rationalizes the wrong value

defects.match: func (s *Store) Entry(ctx context.Context, id int64) (Entry, error) {
defects.note: memo is nullable (schema.sql, and Transfer inserts NULLIF($3, '')), and Scan into a string fails on NULL; Entry errors for every entry without a memo. COALESCE as Entries does, or sql.NullString
the page starts at the cursor row itself while the doc says after it, so the last entry of each page is the first of the next; > $2, or the caller passes last id + 1
the query selects debit_cents before credit_cents and the scan takes them in the other order; both are BIGINT, so nothing fails and every statement shows debits as credits

defects.match: `SELECT balance_cents FROM accounts WHERE id = $1`, to)
defects.note: the destination balance is read without FOR UPDATE and written back as an absolute value computed in Go; two transfers into one account commit the same starting balance plus their own amount and one of them is lost. balance_cents + $1, as the debit side does

defects.match: func (s *Store) Transfer(ctx context.Context, from, to, amount int64, memo string) (int64, error) {
defects.note: from == to is not refused; the source row is debited relatively and then overwritten with the balance read before the debit plus amount, so Transfer(a, a, x) ends with balance + x: a self-transfer mints money. Refuse from == to before touching the database
